tip: Modal verb 'können' is in position 2, the main verb 'sprechen' goes to the very end!
Yes/No question: Modal verb first, main verb at the end.
'können' is irregular. The 'er' form is exactly the same as the 'ich' form (kann).
'leider' means unfortunately. Main verb at the end.
The 'wir' form of modal verbs is identical to the infinitive.
Modal verb 'müssen' (must/have to) pushes 'arbeiten' to the end.
'müssen' changes vowel from 'ü' to 'u' for ich/du/er/sie/es.
translation_en: Do you have to study tomorrow?
He has to go to the doctor.

tip: 'einkaufen' is the main verb here and stays in its infinitive form at the end.
translation_en: We have to shop for groceries.
Do you have to go now?

tip: 'aufräumen' is a separable verb. Prefix 'auf' goes to the end.
translation_en: I am tidying up the room.

tip: With a modal verb, the separable verb DOES NOT split. The whole verb goes to the end.
translation_en: I must tidy up the room.
We watch TV on the weekend.

tip: With a modal verb, 'fernsehen' stays whole at the end of the sentence.
translation_en: I want to watch TV in the evenings.

sentence: Ich lade dich zur Party ein.
translation_en: I am inviting you to the party.

tip: Time in Position 1 -> Verb in Position 2 -> Subject pushed to Position 3.
Use 'am' (an dem) for all days of the week.

sentence: Am Freitag fängt das Wochenende an.

tip: Two verbs: conjugated 'gehen' in pos 2, infinitive 'tanzen' at the end.
Use 'im' (in dem) for all months. Time first -> Verb second.
'Geburtstag haben' means to have a birthday.
translation_en: In February I have my birthday.
In May we have a vacation.

sentence: Im Juli fahren wir ans Meer.
translation_en: In July we travel to the sea.

tip: 'ab' means 'starting from'. Verb stays in position 2.
translation_en: Starting Monday, I will do sports.

sentence: Ab acht Uhr bin ich im Büro.
tip: 'ab' can also be used for clock times.
translation_en: From eight o'clock I am in the office.

sentence: Ab morgen lerne ich jeden Tag.
translation_en: Starting tomorrow, I will study every day.

tip: Adding 's' to parts of the day means 'in the evenings' / 'every evening'.
translation_en: In the evenings I watch TV.

sentence: Mittags esse ich in der Kantine.
translation_en: At noon I eat in the cafeteria.
At night I sleep eight hours.

tip: 'Rad fahren' (to ride a bike). 'Rad' goes to the end like a separable prefix.
translation_en: I like to ride a bike.

tip: 'wandern' means to hike. Goes to the end after 'gehen'.
translation_en: We go hiking on the weekend.

tip: 'Computerspiele' is the plural noun for computer games.
Instruments do not take an article with 'spielen'.
translation_en: She plays the piano very well.
I do aerobics in the gym.

tip: 'in die' implies movement towards the disco.
translation_en: Are you coming to the disco?

sentence: Wir gehen heute in den Club.
tip: 'in den' implies movement towards the club (masculine accusative).
translation_en: We are going to the club today.
I have a lot of free time.

sentence: Was machst du in der Freizeit?
tip: 'in der' is dative indicating a state/time.
translation_en: What do you do in your free time?

tip: 'posten' is an English loanword adapted to German grammar.
'Zum Beispiel' is a very common phrase meaning 'for example'.

translation_en: I am writing a WhatsApp message.
I like listening to classical music.

tip: Musical genres usually do not take articles.
translation_en: She listens to pop and rock.
We are going to a musical.
We are going to the theater today.

sentence: Rufen Sie im Notfall den Arzt.
translation_en: In an emergency, call the doctor.
I am driving to the airport.
When are you at the airport?
We are looking for new staff.
He works in the call center.

tip: Compound noun from the vocabulary list.
translation_en: What is your body mass index?

sentence: Was ist das für ein Ausdruck?
translation_en: What kind of expression is that?
We are sitting in a circle.

tip: Modal verb pushing the infinitive 'waschen' to the end.

translation_en: I still have to get gas today.

tip: 'vorlesen' (to read aloud) is a separable verb.
'wissen' (to know a fact) is an irregular verb.
translation_en: I do not know the answer.
